source_refs.note: Exercise 10.3, Question 2: book pages 194-195 (PDF 199-200); no answer key entry (proofs); (v) holds only where its right side is positive, boxed; checked with sympy and the solution book (PDF 936-951).

blocks.explanation:
A difference of cot and tan must become a double-angle cot.
Plan: write both in sin and cos, take a common denominator, then spot \(\cos 2\alpha\) on top and \(\frac{1}{2}\sin 2\alpha\) below.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \cot\alpha - \tan\alpha\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 2\cot 2\alpha\).
Method: Change to sin and cos; use \(\cos 2\alpha = \cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha\) and \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\).

Common denominator
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha} - \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha}{\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}\]
Why: The common denominator is \(\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\).

Use double-angle formulas
\[= \dfrac{\cos 2\alpha}{\tfrac{1}{2}\sin 2\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{2\cos 2\alpha}{\sin 2\alpha} = 2\cot 2\alpha\]
Why: \(\sin\alpha\cos\alpha = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2\alpha\); and \(\frac{\cos}{\sin} = \cot\).

blocks.explanation:
Double angles on the left, a single angle on the right.
Plan: open \(\sin 2\alpha\) and use \(1 + \cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha\), then cancel.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\sin 2\alpha}{1 + \cos 2\alpha}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan\alpha\).
Method: \(\sin 2\alpha = 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) and \(1 + \cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha\) (from \(\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1\)).

Open both double angles
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha}{2\cos^2\alpha}\]
Why: The form \(2\cos^2\alpha - 1\) is chosen because the 1 cancels with the 1 already present.

Cancel
\[= \dfrac{\sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha} = \tan\alpha\]
Why: \(2\cos\alpha\) cancels from top and bottom.

blocks.explanation:
The right side has a half angle, so we treat \(\alpha\) as double of \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\).
Plan: \(1 - \cos\alpha = 2\sin^2\frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(\sin\alpha = 2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\), then cancel.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{1 - \cos\alpha}{\sin\alpha}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan\frac{\alpha}{2}\).
Method: Double-angle formulas with angle \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\): \(\cos\alpha = 1 - 2\sin^2\frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(\sin\alpha = 2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\).

Write everything with \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\)
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin^2\frac{\alpha}{2}}{2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}\]
Why: \(\alpha = 2 \cdot \frac{\alpha}{2}\), so the double-angle formulas apply.

Cancel
\[= \dfrac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}} = \tan\dfrac{\alpha}{2}\]
Why: \(2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\) cancels.

blocks.explanation:
The right side has double angles; the left side has single angles.
Plan: multiply the left side top and bottom by \(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha\) so that the bottom becomes \(\cos 2\alpha\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sec 2\alpha - \tan 2\alpha\).
Method: \((\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)^2 = 1 - \sin 2\alpha\) and \((\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)(\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha) = \cos 2\alpha\).

Multiply top and bottom by \(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha\)
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)^2}{\cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha}\]
Why: The bottom becomes a difference of squares.

Simplify top and bottom
\[(\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha)^2 = 1 - 2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\]
\[= 1 - \sin 2\alpha\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1 - \sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha}\]
Why: \(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha = 1\) and \(\cos^2\alpha - \sin^2\alpha = \cos 2\alpha\).

Split the fraction
\[= \dfrac{1}{\cos 2\alpha} - \dfrac{\sin 2\alpha}{\cos 2\alpha}\]
\[= \sec 2\alpha - \tan 2\alpha\]
Why: Divide each term by \(\cos 2\alpha\).

blocks.explanation:
The right side uses \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\), so we write \(1 \pm \sin\alpha\) as perfect squares in \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\).
Plan: \(1 = \sin^2\frac{\alpha}{2} + \cos^2\frac{\alpha}{2}\) and \(\sin\alpha = 2\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\), then take the square root.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \sqrt{\frac{1 + \sin\alpha}{1 - \sin\alpha}}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} + \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} - \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}\).
Method: Write \(s = \sin\frac{\alpha}{2}\), \(c = \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}\). Then \(1 + \sin\alpha = (s + c)^2\) and \(1 - \sin\alpha = (s - c)^2\).

Make \(1 + \sin\alpha\) a perfect square
\[1 + \sin\alpha = s^2 + c^2 + 2sc\]
\[= (s + c)^2\]
Why: \(s^2 + c^2 = 1\) and \(2sc = \sin\alpha\) (double angle with \(\frac{\alpha}{2}\)).

Make \(1 - \sin\alpha\) a perfect square
\[1 - \sin\alpha = s^2 + c^2 - 2sc\]
\[= (s - c)^2\]
Why: The same idea with a minus sign.

Take the square root
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \sqrt{\dfrac{(s + c)^2}{(s - c)^2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{s + c}{s - c}\]
Why: The root of a square gives back the quantity, provided \(\frac{s + c}{s - c}\) is positive (see the correction below). This is the printed right side.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: As printed, this identity is true only when its right side is positive, for example \(\frac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \frac{3\pi}{2}\). For acute \(\alpha\) it fails: at \(\alpha = 0\) the left side is \(1\) but the right side is \(\frac{0 + 1}{0 - 1} = -1\). In general the left side equals \(\left|\frac{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} + \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2} - \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}}\right|\); for \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}\) the right side should be \(\frac{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} + \sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}{\cos\frac{\alpha}{2} - \sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}\).

blocks.explanation:
Reciprocal ratios with \(\theta\) and \(2\theta\) on the left; a half angle on the right.
Plan: change to sin and cos, simplify to \(\frac{1 + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\), then use half-angle forms.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\operatorname{cosec}\theta + 2\operatorname{cosec} 2\theta}{\sec\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \cot\frac{\theta}{2}\).
Method: \(\operatorname{cosec} 2\theta = \frac{1}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}\); then \(1 + \cos\theta = 2\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2}\) and \(\sin\theta = 2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\).

Change to sin and cos
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \cos\theta\left[\dfrac{1}{\sin\theta} + \dfrac{2}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta}\right]\]
Why: Dividing by \(\sec\theta\) is multiplying by \(\cos\theta\); \(\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\).

Multiply out
\[= \dfrac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta} + \dfrac{1}{\sin\theta}\]
\[= \dfrac{1 + \cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\]
Why: In the second term \(2\cos\theta\) cancels.

Use half-angle forms
\[= \dfrac{2\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2}}{2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos\frac{\theta}{2}}{\sin\frac{\theta}{2}} = \cot\dfrac{\theta}{2}\]
Why: \(\cos\theta = 2\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} - 1\) and the double-angle form of \(\sin\theta\); then cancel.

blocks.explanation:
After writing in sin and cos, the top becomes \(\cos(2\alpha - \alpha)\).
Plan: common denominator, then the fundamental law \(\cos(a - b) = \cos a\cos b + \sin a\sin b\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= 1 + \tan\alpha\tan 2\alpha\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sec 2\alpha\).
Method: Change to sin and cos; use \(\cos 2\alpha\cos\alpha + \sin 2\alpha\sin\alpha = \cos(2\alpha - \alpha)\).

Common denominator
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 1 + \dfrac{\sin\alpha\sin 2\alpha}{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha + \sin\alpha\sin 2\alpha}{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}\]
Why: Write 1 as \(\frac{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}\).

Use the fundamental law
\[= \dfrac{\cos(2\alpha - \alpha)}{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}\]
\[= \dfrac{\cos\alpha}{\cos\alpha\cos 2\alpha}\]
Why: \(\cos a\cos b + \sin a\sin b = \cos(a - b)\) with \(a = 2\alpha\), \(b = \alpha\).

Cancel
\[= \dfrac{1}{\cos 2\alpha} = \sec 2\alpha\]
Why: \(\cos\alpha\) cancels.

blocks.explanation:
The bottom has \(\cos 3\theta\); the triple-angle formula turns it into powers of \(\cos\theta\).
Plan: show \(\cos\theta + \cos 3\theta = 2\cos\theta\cos 2\theta\), then divide.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{2\sin\theta\sin 2\theta}{\cos\theta + \cos 3\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan 2\theta\tan\theta\).
Method: \(\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta\) (Section 10.6) and \(2\cos^2\theta - 1 = \cos 2\theta\).

Simplify the denominator
\[\cos\theta + \cos 3\theta = \cos\theta + 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta\]
\[= 4\cos^3\theta - 2\cos\theta\]
\[= 2\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1)\]
\[= 2\cos\theta\cos 2\theta\]
Why: Triple-angle formula, then take out \(2\cos\theta\).

Divide
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{2\sin\theta\sin 2\theta}{2\cos\theta\cos 2\theta}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} \cdot \dfrac{\sin 2\theta}{\cos 2\theta}\]
\[= \tan\theta\tan 2\theta\]
Why: The 2 cancels; each sin over its own cos is a tan.

blocks.explanation:
Each fraction simplifies nicely with the triple-angle formulas.
Plan: divide \(\sin 3\theta\) by \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos 3\theta\) by \(\cos\theta\), then subtract.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin\theta} - \frac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 2\).
Method: \(\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta\) and \(\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta\).

Simplify each fraction
\[\dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin\theta} = 3 - 4\sin^2\theta\]
\[\dfrac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos\theta} = 4\cos^2\theta - 3\]
Why: Every term of each triple-angle formula has the factor \(\sin\theta\) or \(\cos\theta\).

Subtract
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 3 - 4\sin^2\theta - 4\cos^2\theta + 3\]
\[= 6 - 4(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)\]
\[= 6 - 4 = 2\]
Why: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).

blocks.explanation:
The same two fractions as part (ix), but added.
Plan: simplify each with the triple-angle formulas, add, then use \(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos\theta} + \frac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 4\cos 2\theta\).
Method: Triple-angle formulas for \(\sin 3\theta\) and \(\cos 3\theta\).

Simplify each fraction
\[\dfrac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos\theta} = 4\cos^2\theta - 3\]
\[\dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin\theta} = 3 - 4\sin^2\theta\]
Why: As in part (ix).

Add
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 4\cos^2\theta - 3 + 3 - 4\sin^2\theta\]
\[= 4(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)\]
\[= 4\cos 2\theta\]
Why: The 3s cancel; \(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta\).

blocks.explanation:
Half angles on the left, a full angle on the right.
Plan: write \(s = \sin\frac{\theta}{2}\), \(c = \cos\frac{\theta}{2}\); simplify top and bottom separately.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\tan\frac{\theta}{2} + \cot\frac{\theta}{2}}{\cot\frac{\theta}{2} - \tan\frac{\theta}{2}}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \sec\theta\).
Method: In terms of \(s, c\): \(\tan\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{s}{c}\), \(\cot\frac{\theta}{2} = \frac{c}{s}\). Then \(s^2 + c^2 = 1\) and \(c^2 - s^2 = \cos\theta\).

Simplify the numerator
\[\dfrac{s}{c} + \dfrac{c}{s} = \dfrac{s^2 + c^2}{sc} = \dfrac{1}{sc}\]
Why: Common denominator \(sc\); \(s^2 + c^2 = 1\).

Simplify the denominator
\[\dfrac{c}{s} - \dfrac{s}{c} = \dfrac{c^2 - s^2}{sc} = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{sc}\]
Why: \(\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} - \sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} = \cos\theta\) (double angle with \(\frac{\theta}{2}\)).

Divide
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{1/(sc)}{\cos\theta/(sc)}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\cos\theta} = \sec\theta\]
Why: The common \(sc\) cancels.

blocks.explanation:
Unlike parts (ix)-(x), the denominators are swapped, so a common denominator is better than the triple-angle formulas.
Plan: common denominator; the top is \(\cos(3\theta - \theta)\); the bottom is \(\frac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{\sin 3\theta}{\cos\theta} + \frac{\cos 3\theta}{\sin\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 2\cot 2\theta\).
Method: \(\cos 3\theta\cos\theta + \sin 3\theta\sin\theta = \cos(3\theta - \theta)\) and \(\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta\).

Common denominator
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sin 3\theta\sin\theta + \cos 3\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}\]
Why: Cross-multiply over \(\sin\theta\cos\theta\).

Use the fundamental law and the double angle
\[= \dfrac{\cos(3\theta - \theta)}{\tfrac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta}\]
\[= \dfrac{2\cos 2\theta}{\sin 2\theta} = 2\cot 2\theta\]
Why: \(\cos a\cos b + \sin a\sin b = \cos(a - b)\) with \(a = 3\theta\), \(b = \theta\).

blocks.explanation:
Both sides can be written in terms of \(\sin^2 2\theta\); we reduce each side to the same expression.
Plan: left side with \(\cos 4\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2 2\theta\); right side with \(\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta = 1 - \frac{1}{2}\sin^2 2\theta\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{3 + \cos 4\theta}{1 - \cos 4\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \frac{1}{2}\left(\tan^{2}\theta + \cot^{2}\theta\right)\).
Method: Let \(u = \sin^2 2\theta\). Show both sides equal \(\frac{2 - u}{u}\).

Left side
\[\cos 4\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2 2\theta = 1 - 2u\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{3 + 1 - 2u}{1 - 1 + 2u}\]
\[= \dfrac{4 - 2u}{2u} = \dfrac{2 - u}{u}\]
Why: Double-angle formula with angle \(2\theta\).

Right side: common denominator
\[\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta = \dfrac{\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta}{\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta}\]
Why: \(\frac{\sin^2}{\cos^2} + \frac{\cos^2}{\sin^2}\) over \(\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\).

Write the right side with \(u\)
\[\sin^4\theta + \cos^4\theta\]
\[= (\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta)^2\]
\[\quad - 2\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta\]
\[= 1 - \tfrac{1}{2}u\]
\[\sin^2\theta\cos^2\theta = \tfrac{1}{4}u\]
Why: \(a^2 + b^2 = (a + b)^2 - 2ab\); \(\sin\theta\cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2\theta\), so its square is \(\frac{1}{4}u\).

Finish the right side
\[\text{R.H.S.} = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1 - \frac{1}{2}u}{\frac{1}{4}u}\]
\[= \dfrac{2(1 - \frac{1}{2}u)}{u} = \dfrac{2 - u}{u}\]
Why: \(\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{4} = 2\). Both sides equal \(\frac{2 - u}{u}\), so L.H.S. = R.H.S.

blocks.explanation:
\(1 \pm \sin 2\theta\) are perfect squares, and \(\frac{1 + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\theta}\) is \(\tan(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta)\).
Plan: perfect squares, divide by \(\cos\theta\), then the formula for \(\tan(a + b)\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \frac{1 + \sin 2\theta}{1 - \sin 2\theta}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= \tan^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\).
Method: \(1 \pm \sin 2\theta = (\cos\theta \pm \sin\theta)^2\) and \(\tan(a + b) = \frac{\tan a + \tan b}{1 - \tan a\tan b}\) with \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\).

Perfect squares
\[1 + \sin 2\theta = (\cos\theta + \sin\theta)^2\]
\[1 - \sin 2\theta = (\cos\theta - \sin\theta)^2\]
Why: \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1\) and \(2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \sin 2\theta\).

Divide top and bottom by \(\cos\theta\)
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \left(\dfrac{\cos\theta + \sin\theta}{\cos\theta - \sin\theta}\right)^2\]
\[= \left(\dfrac{1 + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\theta}\right)^2\]
Why: \(\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \tan\theta\).

Recognise \(\tan(\frac{\pi}{4} + \theta)\)
\[\dfrac{1 + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\theta} = \dfrac{\tan\frac{\pi}{4} + \tan\theta}{1 - \tan\frac{\pi}{4}\tan\theta}\]
\[= \tan\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \tan^2\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4} + \theta\right)\]
Why: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1\), then the formula for \(\tan(a + b)\).

blocks.explanation:
Four angles that pair up: \(\frac{7\pi}{8} = \pi - \frac{\pi}{8}\), \(\frac{5\pi}{8} = \pi - \frac{3\pi}{8}\), and \(\frac{3\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{8}\).
Plan: reduce everything to \(\frac{\pi}{8}\), then \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\).
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \cos^{2}\frac{\pi}{8} + \cos^{2}\frac{3\pi}{8} + \cos^{2}\frac{5\pi}{8} + \cos^{2}\frac{7\pi}{8}\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 2\).
Method: Allied angles: \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\) (the square removes the sign) and \(\cos(\frac{\pi}{2} - x) = \sin x\).

Pair the last two with the first two
\[\cos^2\tfrac{7\pi}{8} = \cos^2\left(\pi - \tfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \cos^2\tfrac{\pi}{8}\]
\[\cos^2\tfrac{5\pi}{8} = \cos^2\left(\pi - \tfrac{3\pi}{8}\right) = \cos^2\tfrac{3\pi}{8}\]
Why: \(\cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x\), and squaring removes the minus sign.

Collect
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2\cos^2\tfrac{\pi}{8} + 2\cos^2\tfrac{3\pi}{8}\]
Why: Each square now appears twice.

Use the co-ratio
\[\cos\tfrac{3\pi}{8} = \cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - \tfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \sin\tfrac{\pi}{8}\]
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2\left(\cos^2\tfrac{\pi}{8} + \sin^2\tfrac{\pi}{8}\right)\]
\[= 2(1) = 2\]
Why: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) is an odd multiple, so cos changes to sin; then \(\sin^2 + \cos^2 = 1\).
